classification.difficultyReason: Derive the radius from the centre and a circumference point before writing the circle equation.

content.prompt: Find the equation of the circle shown below.

spec.description: Unshaded first-quadrant circle, labelled centre and upper-right circumference point, positive axes with arrowheads and no numerical ticks or radius line. Decorative source red outline is rendered black.
spec.mathematics: Centre C(4,4); point P(6,7) lies on the circle. Radius is derived internally from these givens and is not labelled in the question.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied centre and point coordinates are visible.

answer.worked:
The centre is $C(4,4)$. Using the point $P(6,7)$,
$$\begin{align*}r&=CP\\r&=\sqrt{(6-4)^2+(7-4)^2}\\r&=\sqrt{13}.\end{align*}$$
Therefore the circle has equation
$$(x-4)^2+(y-4)^2=13.$$
